previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for a significant drop in hemoglobin from 9.0 to 7.2, initially attributed to a recent episode of bright red diarrhea. She received three units of packed red blood cells and was stabilized. Evaluation revealed a fungal infection (Candida albicans) at her dialysis catheter exit site, prompting removal of the left tunneled catheter. A temporary femoral catheter was placed when the right internal jugular vein was found to be blocked, followed by successful placement of a new permanent catheter in the left jugular vein. She developed a transient fever, but blood cultures were negative, and antibiotics were discontinued. A left pleural effusion was noted on imaging, possibly related to heart failure or infection, but remained stable without intervention. Gastroenterology recommended outpatient evaluation for GI bleeding, as colonoscopy was deferred due to lack of IV access and stable labs. She completed a course of fluconazole for the fungal infection and was discharged home with services to continue follow-up care.
